tips.comment: Jowddah finished second in all 3 starts as a juvenile but returned this season with a maiden win at Newcastle in April and followed up last month on handicap debut at Yarmouth. He is up just 3 lbs for that, so has a good chance of bringing up the hat trick.

Treasure was quite highly tried at the end of last season, and drops back in grade here. Ralph Beckett has a good way with his fillies, and might have found an opportunity here to boost Treasure's confidence.

6yo irish mare Yokkell has won her last race over 1m1/2f at Nottingham. This was on first run for new trainer and after a 6 months break, so should be open for more improvement. Only 3lbs higher for that easy win and stays in the same class. Should be in the mix.
Won over half a furlong further making all on good to soft ground at Musselburgh last time out and the third horse home in that race, Zapphire, won last month over a mile to boost the form.

Four career runs from the 3yo. Back from a 9 month break with a big run on his handicap debut six weeks ago, 3rd and beaten under a length in the end. The 4th won next time out, the 2nd has won twice since and rated much higher now. Room for improvement for the selection and he’s running off the same mark.

I have had a woeful month of May but let's start June off with a change of fortune. French Haven had shown very little but on her third handicap start dropping back to 8f and with Jamie Spencer on board she was very game coming from last to first under the head waiter. That was a fillies 0-68 and today she is not against her own sex but it is a 0-62 which on paper is easier. Unusual for a Charlie Johnston horse to get held up but it worked last time and if the same tactics are applied again she might just follow up.

Hugely improved performance to finish 3rd at Southwell on the all-weather after returning from a long break for the first time since debut. The long distance is expected to suit here, and has a decent high draw. The gelding operation has already shown signs of making a big difference.
Beaten 7 length at Doncaster last time but has shown signs of potential. Now fitted with a tongue tie, could exceed expectations if at its best.

Take an EW chance on 3yo irish filly Take The Boat. She is actually in good form since February with 4 wins in 7 races. Didn't get much luck in the running in her last two runs and she wasn't disgraced on her only turf start when 4th of 7. Could be good for a little surprise here.

This C G Cox trained colt must be going well at home as he was a well-backed favourite for his racecourse debut over five furlongs on good to firm ground at Salisbury, only to be beaten a neck behind the A M Balding trained Comical Point. So with that run under his belt, he can go one place better today with David Probert booked to ride.
Ameeq was not disgraced on his debut at Beverley where he placed 5th. He should have come on for that run and further progress is a possibility.
Bay of Dreams has shown consistent form in its last three races, which included two place finishes and a victory. He has won over this distance, albeit on the all-weather course.

3yo irish gelding Glitter Code is still a maiden after 10 races but has knocked at the door lto when runner-up over 1m at Yarmouth. Is on a dangerous mark and this one doesn't look stronger than lto. Will be in the mix.
Still a maiden, Adversary has run well in defeat on the All Weather. He is now making his turf debut, and he would not need much improvement to figure here.

Westgate Warrior is a 3-year-old gelding trained by Roy Bowring. He made an encouraging stable debut last time out when beaten 3 lengths at Southwell. He is making his handicap debut off top weight of 62, having posted a career-high RPR of 68 on his last start. It could be a good time to catch Westgate Warrior, given the yard's current form, winning with their last two runners, Jeans Maite at 7-2 and Back From Dubai at 7-1. He should give us a run for our money under Lewis Edmunds.

Lightly raced maiden who gained valuable experience over C&D LTO despite finishing 9th of 10 earlier this month. So hoping that experience, along with dropped mark and drop down in class, will be enough to cause an upset tomorrow.

The Crafty Mole should be spot on after two runs so far this season. He ran well at Haydock last time, and this course and distance look ideal for him. The yard is in tremendous form, and The Crafty Mole looks better than most of these.

Plenty of course and distance form on show here. Not much between Rock N Roll Pinkie for local trainer Ivan Furtado and Expressionless, who won the race last year. That was off a handicap mark of 70, and that performance was later boosted when he went on to win a Racing League class 3 race at Yarmouth worth £50,000 off a mark of 73. He's rated 72 today but has conditions to suit, whereas the Furtado horse needs easier ground. 5/1 seems a fair price.

Gallant Lion won comfortably in an apprentice handicap at Chepstow over twelve furlongs on Friday. If fully recovered, he could follow up without a penalty under the same rider, Ryan Kavanagh, claiming five pounds here over an extra two furlongs. He won eased down after going clear to be only half a length ahead at the line.
Did it nicely here latest and the softer ground should not spoil his chance of a follow-up. Trip, track and ground are proven.

Disappointing on her return to action at Newbury. The return to a longer trip should be a help to her, and she is far too well-bred to think that 66 will be the limit of her ability, especially given that her powerful trainer continues with her.

Decent comeback from a break to take 3rd at Doncaster by less than a length off the winner. A regular here at Nottingham with two wins and a second place finish from five runs. Goes unpunished for last time out.

I'm not a big Rab Havlin fan, to be honest, so I can only put this one up each way. If Havlin has a go at it and tries, it could win. If Havlin does what he often does and just picks up his place money, we could actually be out of the top three.

Jonny Portman is enjoying a great season, and his Russian Rumour looks weighted rather nicely to hopefully score on her second start of the season. Drops back into a Class 5 after a pipe opener in an Ascot Class 4 when 5th of 8. Useful claimed Jack Callan takes off 7lb, which effectively leaves my selection off a mark of 61. Has won off 62 & 66, so looks well weighted and can go close.

Angel Shared was sent off 6/1 for a class 2 handicap at Chester last time out. She was below form there, but the trainer said the track didn't suit. She drops in grade today and is on slightly easier ground, which is sure to suit. She should go well.
Nad Alshiba Green was 3rd behind Sugar Hill Babe over course and distance three weeks ago. She could go well again and hit the frame in a wide-open race.
Only just got beaten last time out, up a 1lb but holding form. Top balanced pick. Likes the going and distance, should go close today.

Three career runs for the 3yo filly. Back from a 6 month break with a nice novice stakes win four weeks ago, over this 5f trip - her turf debut that day. Picking up nicely in the final furlong and winning a shade cosy - decent RPR rating. Still unexposed and an opening handicap mark of 74 should give her a chance.

Jacquelina could be coming to hand with this being her fourth run. She just got tired at Chepstow on her last run, finishing in third place. Grace McEntee can get the fractions right if aiming to lead, which can see the mare running a big race off 77.

Smooth Silesie is a 4yo filly trained by Lisa Williamson. She did well for the yard in 2024, winning five times, and sits just 2lb above her last winning mark, so is well-weighted to make an impression. She is also a CD winner, which bodes well, and seemingly handles a bit of cut in the ground. She can figure today under Lewis Edmunds at 18-1.
This is a really tough race to call, with both Without Berlington and Outlandish having serious claims. But I think the progressive Penywern should just sneak this.

One More Chrome is a twice-raced 3-year-old gelding trained by B F Brookhouse. He showed promise on debut, finishing 6/11, beaten 7.5 lengths behind Starzintheireyes, who has subsequently won a Group 3 race. He is out of a dam that won a listed race and was rated 106, and is related to four individual winners, three of which posted career-high RPRs of 99, 99, and 100. B F Brookhouse also does well at Nottingham, winning with 6 of his last 19 runners and placing 12. One More Chrome should have matured during the absence and go well under the talented Robert Havlin.

4yo irish gelding Sustained was a good 2nd of 9 lto over 7f at Wolverhampton. This came after a 242 day break, so should be even sharper here today on his turf reapppearence. Wasn't disgraced on his two career runs on grass and he is on a handy mark, so should be in the mix.
Previous course and distance winner. On a 5 lb higher mark, still looks a solid contender and likes a bit of cut in the ground, so a good each-way chance. Stall 4 works out well also.

Owned and trained by Robert Eddery and won nicely under Jack Callan at Yarmouth in April over 8f and went up 6lb for that. Up in class today, but as such, gets in off bottom weight and with Jack taking off the 7lb again, receives a huge amount of weight from his 12 rivals and makes plenty of each-way appeal.

Charencey has been below form on the AW of late, but I think he's a better horse on turf. He dead-heated at Doncaster last season off a mark of 73, and he is now down to 66. With potential improvement for switching to turf, he's very well handicapped. He ran well after an 88-day break last season, so it can be seen as a positive that he's coming here fresh.
Presumably required the effort when defeated by 6 lengths in a handicap on first start of the season. Likely to be in better shape now.

Owned and trained by Roy Bowring, Cliffcake has won 11 and placed 4 times from 48 runs. The 7-year-old son of Canford Cliffs also has 1 win and 1 second place from 2 starts over C&D. Admittedly, he has disappointed in his last 2 runs, but if running today with the handbrake off, he has the ability to win in this grade, off this mark, over this trip, and on this ground.
Howth, a former decent stayer on the flat, impressed with his debut win over hurdles at Market Rasen after a long absence from the track. He should follow up at Fakenham.
High Court Judge takes on previous winner Howth in what could be a tactical race between the pair. He beat a previous winner in its last race, and it could add another win to its growing reputation.

A fairish flat performer with a good place stats of 14 from 35 (also won one race), Francesi makes his hurdling debut today. If there had been one or two runners in this, I definitely would've gone e.w. because of the trainer's impressive place strike-rate at this course.
Won by 16 lengths in a 2m 2f handicap at Fontwell last time out. He looked really impressive the way he went clear, and hopefully, he will follow up that with a win today.

The model I run suggests Tara Iti can win this race. Tara Iti lines up with a very comparable RPR in what looks like a fairly open race. Tara Iti carries over one stone less than the current market favorite around this 2m trip and comes here in decent form, having placed well 7 days ago. Form figures of 21F-22 and looks to add another first here today. The model has issued a 'moderate' stake indicator, which translates to a 1pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This result has been driven by Tara Iti getting over the line first with a reasonable gap back to second in the race simulation, but with short odds at 2/1, it doesn't represent great value.
Likely needed the run when fourth, beaten 11 lengths in a 2m4f handicap hurdle at Huntingdon last time. A shorter trip should suit.

This doesn't look like a strong race, and Abingworth has good recent form. The angle with him is that he is having his first run for James Owen. The trainer has an excellent record when taking horses over from another yard, and he is also in great form at the moment. I think this horse could be rated much higher in a few months' time.

The model I run suggests Trapista can win this race. Trapista lines up here with the highest RPR of the 6 runner field and has rock bottom official ranking. This suggests Trapista carries weight far less than the potential he has to run well. The difference in weight to the other horses ranges from 7 lbs all the way up to over 1 stone 9 lbs (!). Trapista ran well 21 days ago to come a decent second over this distance and looks to get over the line first today. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Well, Bearren in a 3m 2f handicap chase at Plumpton last time. But the race on 1 Feb was worth noting. A shorter trip may help.

The oldest in the field and the longest off the course. So much for the negatives. The trainer, like his father before him, is well able to ready a horse for a top effort after a lay-off. Has the best of the time, weight and class rates.
Romped home last time out in her first handicpa race and although she's gone up 10 pond in the weight for that win she looks more than able to improve on that race

The model I run suggests an upset from One Man Party. One Man Party lines up here with the highest RPR of the small 5-runner field and has an official ranking that is the lowest of the lot. This subsequently means One Man Party goes out carrying the lowest amount of weight around this ~3m trip. There is a good 1 stone 2 lbs weight difference to the current market leader, and over a 3m distance, that's a lot. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This is largely driven by the small gap back to 2nd in the race simulation.

The model I run suggests Extraordinary Man can win this race. Extraordinary Man lines up here with the highest RPR of this small 4-runner race and has the second lowest official ranking. This suggests Extraordinary Man is carrying weight less than what his potential can be. The weight difference here to the top of the market is one stone, which could be telling over a 2m trip. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, largely driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Tumbled down in the weights, ran here in a respectable 2nd at 85 in a 5-runner event. With all 3 career wins coming from today's jockey, expecting a big run at a mark of 72.

Still a maiden after 26 races under rules, but was 2nd in seven races and 3rd in another six. So, Gone In Sixty has some talent and was unlucky in running last time when having to switch going to the last flight. Alice Stevens is a decent rider despite her five-pound allowance for this Lady Riders' handicap hurdle. Looks to have a decent chance of finally getting his first win.
Course and distance winner on debut 2 runs back in February, going clear impressively. Disappointed last time on turf, but that was a listed race. This is easier.

She's A Warrior returns after a break of 230 days. All her runs last year were at Kempton, and her record is a win and two places from three runs, all over a mile. She is now being upped in trip, and further progress is likely.

Sole career win came over today's course and distance back in March. Ran another solid race last time out when taking the runner-up spot here over the same trip earlier this month. Looks a value bet for each way purposes at least today with the plum draw in stall one.

The 3yo filly was only beaten a nk two weeks ago, her second return run, earning a good rating. Just five career starts and she can take a step forward in this handicap. She is a previous winner on the polytrack.

This one looks overpriced to me. Has ran poorly the last twice on turf, but on AW it's a different story. He was a course and distance winner last September. He also won at Wolves under this jockey, from a 3lb lower mark than today, winning by a length despite trouble in running. I think he has an excellent each-way chance.

Kempton maiden winner who followed up on handicap debut at Wolverhampton in November. Solid placed efforts in three starts since, including when 2nd back from a break at Lingfield. Nudged up another lb and some stamina questions for this longer trip, but should run well nevertheless.

All six career wins have come on all-weather tracks, including five here at Chelmsford, with four of those wins coming over today's trip. Raised three pounds for the most recent win but looks to have strong claims again here despite going up in class.

Beaten a head off this mark of 76 over half a furlong further at Doncaster last month under today's jockey. Has run well here before when an unlucky 4th and a beaten favorite over half a furlong shorter in July 2024 off this mark too.

Has won here in the past, so hoping course experience and drop down in class makes life a little easier tomorrow. Although the mark remains unchanged, it's still only 3lbs higher than the last winning mark.
Where's Freddy was unlucky not to win last time here. He had to go around the weakening rivals and lost some momentum in the process. Rossa Ryan is in the saddle again. Chances!
Shaped well after 7 months off last time. Not ideally placed and ridden for another day, finishing well out wide. Saffie booked and should go close.

Two runs this year for the 4yo. He was a close 2nd of 16 during April on his return, in a useful £18K handicap over this C/D. He won his next start - on turf. Not much higher in weights now and looking like he’s on an upward curve. Good low draw.

All ten career wins have come on all-weather tracks, including one here at Chelmsford. Won at Southwell when last running over today's trip and looks a decent bet for each-way purposes from a handy draw in stall five, with many bookies paying out on extra places.

Now 4lb lower then when finishing 3rd of 8 4 starts ago. That makes him very competitive off a mark of 81. Runs the track well in what looks a wide open race can have a solid enough each way chance here

Just 2 runs to date and incredibly looking to make it a hat-trick of wins in handicap debut tomorrow. In what will also be his course debut and down in trip should make life a bit easier. But 14-month absence and tricky starting mark could be his undoing. But he has a chance if he can overcome this.

Winner at Kempton in October. Mostly solid efforts since, though was a bit below par when 5th at Lingfield last time. Nudged down a lb for that so would be no surprise to see him run well this evening.

Shamrock Bay most probably needed his last run at Nottingham when he returned after a break of 282 days. He is still lightly raced, having won his first two races last year. Could do well now after having had the benefit of a recent run.
Makes polytrack debut, but has run well enough on Tapeta and comes here off the back of a decent 5th in a big York handicap. Looks the one to beat, and the race will be run to suit.
Another one who will get the strong pace he needs. This will be difficult, whacked up 6lb and in a much better race, but he loves it around here and should get a place.

Northcliff really is a speed merchant and I think he can edge it today if he gets the right run. Well treated at these weights and has a favorable draw. Should run well at Chelmsford, course and distance winner. Good jockey and trainer combo.

A very open-looking sprint where Farasi Lane looks a good price at the 10/1 mark. This drop in trip looks like a step in the right direction. He has dropped to a lovely handicap mark and should be able to sit in from his wide draw and get a good toe into the race.

Monsieur Beaulieu was poor last time out at Windsor in a class 3 handicap, but the time before that he was a good 2nd here. He has never been out of the frame in 3 starts at the track, and from 6 starts in this class, he has only been unplaced once. His jockey, Fred Daly, is good value for his claim, and he looks too big with the extra place on offer.
Better on his second start of the season and has been given a wind op since. Is 2lb above his last winning mark but he has a 5lb claimer helping his burden.

Things are not going to plan for the new yard just yet, and much improvement is required after the last time out horror show when 13 of 13 at Newmarket last month. Not among the 7 C&D winners in this field, but the dropped mark now means back down to the last winning mark, which was a win here at a longer distance and dropping down 2 classes tomorrow.

Made racecourse debut over 6f at Newmarket. Despite showing clear signs of inexperience and encountering traffic problems through the race, did well to finish 3rd. Connections switch to the AW for his second start, and with improvement likely following that debut, looks to hold strong claims.

Venetian Lace looks well bred and well drawn for her first race over six furlongs being out of a one mile to ten furlongs Listed winner and Charlie Johnston sends her on the long trip down from Middleham to Chelmsford with every chance from her rail draw.
Our Cody was sent off favorite on her debut but ran very green and didn't pick up when asked. She should be wiser this time. Trainer and jockey combo are doing well lately.

Two nice runs from the 4yo when last seen, 2nd and 3rd in decent handicaps - good RPR ratings. Well clear of the rest in his last race, the form was given a nice boost by the winner since. Comes here fresh after a 5 month break as he goes for this £26K first prize. Possible improvement to come. Good low draw and a strong jockey booking.

Was returning from a six-month absence when making his debut for this yard over 6f at Doncaster at the end of March. Finished a running on 4th, beaten less than 2 lengths, and has since run respectably twice at Newmarket over 6 and 7 furlongs. Beaten in a photo finish last time. Connections switch him to the AW for the first time since joining them, although he is a winner on an AW surface at Dundalk for the previous yard. Every chance of making the frame at least here, kept to that trip.

Richard Hannon's horses are currently outperforming. Signcastle City has been kept on his mark of 86 after two 2nds and a 3rd place so far this season. He won three times last season and looks close to getting his first win of the season. He is ideally drawn on the rail if wanting to go with the pace.

Documenting won his last race of 2024 when winning at Wolverhampton on Boxing Day over seven furlongs. He was then given a break before returning two weeks ago at Thirsk, where he was finishing well to get up into fourth spot. He is down a pound since then but no longer has a three-pound claimer on his back. Last year, he won over today's course and distance from a mark of eighty-nine. Today, he runs off a mark of eighty-eight, and providing he comes on from his last run, he could well finish in the top five.
Very solid looking 4th over at Kempton on his latest run. Dropped 1 lb for that. Distance winner in the past. Solid each way player here.

Probe has won two of his four starts on AW, the last coming over 6 furlongs here at Chelmsford in November '23. That was off a mark of 90, and he is 2 lbs lower here. He won again at Chester in May before only finishing 5th at Thirsk 2 weeks ago. The ground might have been too quick for him there, and back on AW, he looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.
Ridden as if a plan was afoot last time. And with a strong pace all but guaranteed, this is a very strong each-way bet from just a pound higher.

Not seen since December when winning with a fair bit in hand at Kempton, so has winning form on Polytrack, unlike a bunch of these. That form from December looks decent with plenty of winners coming from it, including the prolific MR Baloo. Decent chance in this.

Talented individual who picked up a first win for Jamie Osborne at Wolverhampton in August. Solid efforts thereafter and ran okay on reappearance at Chester, albeit beaten favourite. A step forward from that will surely put him bang there this afternoon.

Never been as far as this 7f but did win here over 6f last Nov. Seen once since and that was on season debut mid April when 5th of 9 at Newmarket when not enjoying the undulations, but was strong at the finish over the stiff 5f. Stepping up in trip, although also into the unknown looks worth exploring and Fantasy Master is a nice price with 5 places on offer with some.

Much improved effort LTO when 6th of 13 at Kempton this month. It helps he's a course winner, which was off a higher mark, and does have bags of ability as evident when achieving 3 consecutive wins back in 2023. But the reality is that it's now been 535 days since the last win. However, the current mark could be crucial, so worth chancing.

All four career wins have come here at Chelmsford, including two over today's trip. Raised five pounds for the latest win earlier this month and looks capable of landing the double, receiving weight all round, stepping up in class.
Makes Polytrack debut. Comes here on the back of 2 narrow defeats, having won from 8lb lower last October. Won't be far away if taking to the surface.
Spring Is Sprung has been upped in the weights after winning at Newmarket a fortnight ago. He should still remain competitive and is one to consider for the frame.

Having finished last season badly out of form, he seemed to bounce back on his reappearance run at Newmarket over 5f, finishing a close-up 4th and wasn’t beaten far on his latest outing at Ascot despite only beating one other rival. He may have found the firm ground against him. That spell of poor form last season has seen his mark fall well below his last winning one, and switched to the AW here, he can’t be ignored.
Strong performance last time out. Impressive on fast ground, runs well on polytrack. Decent jockey and trainer combo that could being fruitful at Chelmsford.
Point to Point winner who has joined a top-class stable for his NH debut. He's very well-bred and, despite a long layoff, looks sure to be fit. The trainer gets plenty of bumper winners.

Diamond Tipp is the most exposed horse in this race. She returned after a seven-month absence to Kilbeggan, placing 13th of 14 back in April. She finished three times second last year and, based on that form, has a chance of a place.

Willie Mullins and Gordon Elliott both have likely candidates for this race, but it could be worth a small interest at the price on Look and Sea. He is a half-brother to Fiddlerontheroof, who achieved a very high rating of 155. His trainer, Martin Brassil, doesn't have the greatest record in bumpers, i.e., 5% over the last 5 years, but that goes up to over 33% for placed horses, and he knows the time of day.

Maiden pointer, finished 7th in a bumper at Cork during NH debut 41 days ago. While a win seems unlikely, the 35/1 odds suggest a potential profit from an each-way bet, especially with the jockeys 7lb claim in play.

Second in two bumper starts, Toad Hall was an easy ten length winner of a maiden hurdle at Downpatrick in March and ran fairly well when fourth of seven in a Class 2 novice hurdle at Cheltenham since (against useful sorts). Challengers are few here (two of the five entered runners ran yesterday). Step up in trip to 3m1f promises to suit (Bob's Back is grand-dam so has a staying pedigree). Paul Townend (SR 17%) rides for Willie Mullins (SR 25%). Looks the likely winner.

Wannabe Royal was down the field in a listed race last time. It has a more reasonable task today. In what essentially looks like a heads-up against Admiral Churchill, I give Wannabe the edge. Winning very well at Limerick and looked to be progressive before that, so it was a shame with the blip last time out.

Won a maiden at Limerick over 7f. The trainer is doing really well and I think he can get the best out of this horse this afternoon. Needs to see if he can handle this distance. Dangerous if he has stamina.
Finished third, beaten 6.5 lengths in its debut over 5f at Naas behind a good horse. Now with a top jockey on board and stepping up in distance. Major claims.
Expecting a better run here, having made debut and finished eighth at the Curragh over this distance, but significant improvement is needed.
Yet to win over fences but has placed in all of the last 6 outings. Has won 3 times over hurdles and no surprise to see getting that first chase win.

The outsider of the field, but John Patrick Ryan could have his mare ready to be accountable as the handicapper has eased her down to a rating of 98. With Daniel King in the plate, she could be sounding out a big run in this handicap.

Sorrentino is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Willie Mullins. He makes his flat debut and is very lightly raced with just two starts in bumpers. He won comfortably in a bumper on May 24, beating Fatal Flaw, Gers, Gigi, and Kate Knows Best, who have all won since. He is a sixth foal related to 4/5 winners on the flat and out of a dam that won her debut and placed in a Group 3. Willie Mullins is also 8/32 wins on the flat at Listowel in the last 10 years. Thus, Sorrentino is my short-priced banker of the day.
Fitness must be taken on trust but everything else looks right. Drops in class, has the time and weights in favour and one of the best amateurs on board.

A reliable jumps winner. Having raced twice on the flat, he came in 6th in a maiden at Bellewstown 57 days prior. With in-form jockey holding a 7lb claim, this 8 year old is a fantastic option for an each-way wager at generous 40/1 odds.
Goin placed last of 15 on his stable and Irish debut at Killarney just under three weeks ago. He had decent form in Germany and may have settled now and could outrun his odds.
I Am River was fancied for his only race so far, a bumper back in January, but he hung left, weakened, and lost his action. He should be given another chance over hurdles.
Was a 10L winner at Sligo on latest outing. Raised 11lb for that, but drop back in trip will suit and should be there or thereabouts.

Hoping to see Paddy Hanlon bouncing out once the flag has been brought down. Hopefully, he will settle into a good stride and be well capable of holding a position to be in the equation come the finishing line, either winning or being placed.

Torquay Road was double entered this weekend and was down to run yesterday, where he was backed from 33/1 into 9's before being scratched before the off. I find that interesting because of the duck-egg form figures. But saying that, he did win seven runs ago when fancied.
There are plenty with good chances in this race, and I can see Still She Blooms at least placing. She has placed in 3 of the last 4 races and should easily repeat that today.

I have fallen for this beautiful grey horse and had such high hopes last time out up to a mile. I even told the jockey what to do to win, but they never listen, haha. Always finishes late and usually fast, but last time out the jockey tried to go through a brick wall of horses to no avail. Back over 7f today in what looks like an easier race but is carrying top weight, which could be a downside. But I still think that white flash finish could be on if the jockey finds the gaps.

Are You In Or Out was four lengths 8th behind Harry The Rogue at Naas in April. She had won her prior race and could be thereabouts again in what is a wide-open affair despite not having the best of draws.
This horse is running off a mark of 37 in this race with the claimer on and will love the going today. I fancy this horse will go very close today.

Aspurofthemoment won a point in November before joining Gavin Cromwell. He has since won handicap hurdles at Gowran in January and Bellewstown in April. He goes chasing here, but with the stable remaining in good form, he looks the most likely winner.

Barry Connel may be happy with the ease in the ground that can suit this bay gelding who is sired by Sir Percy. He could be allowing himself to stride along and capable of picking up when Sean Flanagan says go. Pray he has the turn of foot to put on a show for a big run appearing.

A promising contender. Quite a useful victor at 16f in hurdles. Showed potential with a 6th place finish out of 14 in a novice chase at Tipperary during his first outing over fences 24 days ago. He has the added advantage of a 3lb claim from the jockey. There's a solid opportunity for an each-way profit at 18/1.
Has won two of his last three on the flat, one of which was over this distance at Dundalk in January. Looks likely to improve further.

Empress Alma was 4 1/2 lengths behind Inchiquin Star at Gowran Park eleven days ago. She placed 7th that day, never troubling the leaders, but will have come on for that run and do better now, possibly reversing the form with the winner on that day.

Moved into handicaps last time at Roscommon after three runs in which she had shown a fair level of ability. The last one, prior to her handicap debut, saw her finish 5th of 14 over 10f and was keeping on steadily. Was given a lot to do stepping up to 12f at Roscommon under an apprentice but better is expected here going up further in distance with top jockey booked.

Say It So won 4 times last year, with two coming over hurdles and the final two on the flat at Navan in October and Dundalk in November. He is 5 lbs higher here, but Paddy Harnett claims that back. If ready for his first run in 5 months, he looks a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

QUIZ TEST punted latest and he appeared to peak second-up last term. He has a notable claiming apprentice aboard who rides plenty fancied by different stables much sought after , so sharper for his return run in a more competitive handicap he should be in the mix.
Will do another couple tonight and then regroup. Has run really well the last twice winning and then 2nd lto. That was only a few days ago, so guess they are striking while the iron's hot.

Facethepuckout looks interesting here as he is now 6 lbs below his last winning mark. That was his 6th career win coming last July at Naas. He has only run once this year when unplaced back at Naas in March but has been dropped 4 lbs since. Colin Keane, who has ridden him for 2 of his wins, is back on board. He looks like a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.

White Clover is a 4-year-old filly trained by Joseph G Murphy, a trainer who has 10 wins out of 68 at the track in the last 10 years and won with 4 of his last 11 entries. White Clover is 1 out of 10 wins and is seemingly ground versatile. She has posted a career-high RPR of 68 and runs today off 58. She made an encouraging performance at the Curragh last time out, beaten 2.75 lengths, finishing 5th out of 27 under today's jockey, Gary Carroll, who won on her at Navan. White Clover holds every chance today.

SKILLMAN AVE down at the foot of this handicap is of interest for a powerful in-form dual-purpose Irish yard. She could be well placed by trainer Gavin Cromwell and many handicappers from this yard racing on the level are worth a second look. With the benefit of a reappearance sighter behind her she appeals as a big value play.
Was a winner at Cork in October but has not been anywhere near that level in 3 races since. Now on a career-low mark and holds an each-way chance if rediscovering that form.

This looks good each way. Despite there being 16 runners, I can't see any pace in the race apart from the selection. Cian Collins' 6yo has failed to last home at Fairyhouse and Punchestown in his last two outings, but it'll be a different story around this tight track, especially if, as I hope, he has an easy time of it up front.
Would have been placed if not for falling at the second last at Limerick last time out. This doesn't look too high a standard, so can get off the mark running off only a 2 lbs higher mark.

Thomas Coyle's 6-year-old mare JOHANNA'S JEAN ran respectably enough on her handicap debut 37 days ago, finishing 6th (of 15). She is dropped 2 lbs for that effort to a mark of 91 and gets another 3 lbs shaved off thanks to the jockey booking of Conor Stone-Walsh, who is very good value for his claim and arrives here in fine fettle with a 42.86% place strike rate over the past fortnight. Trainer Thomas Coyle has a 50% place strike rate with his second-time-out handicappers, as well as a 25% place strike rate here in County Westmeath over the past five years. This daughter of DIAMOND BOY shouldn’t worry about the step up in trip, and with an extra 5lb pull, could take another step forward here.

In a wide-open race, a chance is taken on Ballykinar, who is making his handicap debut. He was not disgraced in his last three attempts over hurdles, and the step up in trip will arguably suit him. One for the frame.

RUN FOR COVER runs for a top Irish yard and this later-starting six year old mare is well bred likely still with unlocked potential. She has been given time since a handicap debut sighter likely to establish her optimium trip in this sphere of racing and this yard would have no issues getting one ready to land a few bets in modest company such as this.

Dual-purpose horse who comes here from a slipping mark. Caught the eye 3 runs back, over hurdles, when having his first run for 7 months, given a very tender ride. Comes here after a spin on the turf and looks potentially well handicapped off 91, a net 86 with the jockey's 5lb claim. Each-way chance.

OUR UNCLE JACK has generally been looked after through his career as a now nine year old. He has twice looked around this circuit and a step back up to this trip could be the answer. He appears well treated against what he achieved when winning his maiden hurdle and possibly now coming back to hand he appeals as an each-way play.

SILENT DAWN has had 3 spins this season and looks like someone ready to collect a cheque. He looked a winner jumping the 2nd last LTO here at Kilbeggan but didn’t find enough at the business end. Similar story at Clonmel on his penultimate start, finishing 3rd of 13, and prior to that fell at the last at Clonmel. Adrian Murray’s 6 y/o has given the impression stepping up in trip won't inconvenience him too much, and the 1st time cheekpieces offer hope also.
